data.name: Monitor_Name
data.value: Adaptive Agent for PHD2 — Sky Conditions

data.name: Monitor_Description
data.value:
Continuously watches the sky conditions and the Adaptive Agent's guiding reliability. (It appears under N.I.N.A.'s “Safety Monitor” equipment category — that is N.I.N.A.'s name for the device slot, not this monitor's role.)
Reports UNSAFE when: STAR_LOST persists beyond the configured timeout; sky transparency stays degraded (index-based persistence); NINA telemetry goes stale while the sky was degraded; or the Agent becomes unreachable during an active session. Losing reliable observation is always treated as a risk condition — never as "safe".
This monitor only reports SAFE/UNSAFE — N.I.N.A.'s Sequence Engine always owns the sequence: your end-of-sequence criteria (end time, dawn, altitude) always win, and any running recovery is cancelled automatically the moment the sequence ends. Any safety-aware construct can consume this state; the setup below is the recommended recovery workflow, not the only one.
AUTOMATIC RECOVERY (recommended Advanced Sequencer setup): Trigger On Unsafe └ Before Waiting For Safety └ Recovery probe (Adaptive Agent)
That single instruction is the complete recovery loop: while conditions are unsafe it automatically takes verification exposures (replicating your last light) at the configured cadence — or sooner when the Agent's guide-star SNR hints the sky is recovering — and it ends on its own the moment this monitor returns SAFE, letting the sequence resume. No extra containers, loops or Camera instructions are needed (NINA rejects them inside the trigger anyway).

data.name: Probe_AutoTimeout
data.value: Auto cadence

data.name: Probe_AutoTimeout_Tip
data.value: Recommended. The probe cadence is derived from the Agent's telemetry freshness window minus the probe exposure, so sky data never goes stale between probes — and it never waits more than 3 minutes (field-validated) when the window would allow a faster check. It adapts by itself to your sub length. Uncheck to force a fixed timeout in minutes.

data.name: Probe_FallbackExp
data.value: Fallback exposure (s)

data.name: Probe_FallbackExp_Tip
data.value: Used ONLY if no LIGHT has been saved yet this session (for example right after restarting N.I.N.A.). In every other case the probe replicates the interrupted sub exactly — required by the transparency index, whose star-count comparison is not normalized for exposure time.

data.name: Probe_MinInterval_Tip
data.value: Absolute floor between two probes: it caps the guide-SNR hint too, so a fluctuating hint can never hammer the shutter. This is your control over how many probe frames end up on disk during a long cloud-out.

data.name: Probe_Timeout_Tip
data.value: Fail-safe cadence: how long the loop waits before taking a verification exposure when the guide-SNR hint has not fired earlier. Used only while “Auto cadence” is off.

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Check
data.value: Report unsafe when the guide channel goes silent

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Help
data.value: Watches whether PHD2 is still delivering guide frames at all — not how good the guiding is (that is the engine's job). Legitimate pauses (meridian flip, autofocus, manual stop) are announced by PHD2 and never raise an alarm; a guide camera that dies stops talking instead, and that silence is what this detects. A severe PHD2 alert or a burst of per-frame star errors halves the delay.

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Label
data.value: Sky Conditions — guide channel observability

data.name: Settings_GuidePolls
data.value: Silent → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_GuidePolls_Tip
data.value: Polls of confirmed silence before declaring UNSAFE. Frames flowing again drain the count. Higher = more tolerant of brief gaps.

data.name: Settings_GuideSilence
data.value: Silence threshold (s):

data.name: Settings_GuideSilence_Tip
data.value: Seconds without ANY guide frame (guiding or re-acquisition attempts) before the channel is considered suspect. Halved when corroborated by a severe PHD2 alert or repeated per-frame star errors.

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Label
data.value: Sky Conditions — meridian protection

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Check
data.value: Authorize the mechanical meridian flip during a long unsafe hold

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Help
data.value: Without this, NINA reacts to an unsafe flip deadline by stopping mount tracking — and nothing ever restarts it: the guide star drifts away, probe images trail, and the monitor loses every eye it decides with. The night ends there even if the sky clears (verified on 19/7). This window briefly reports safe so the flip alone can run, then immediately restores the unsafe hold: it protects the monitor's own ability to keep observing, it never judges the sky. Reconsider only if other devices (roof, dome) start consuming this monitor's safe state.

data.name: Settings_MeridianLead
data.value: Open window (min before flip deadline):

data.name: Settings_MeridianLead_Tip
data.value: How many minutes before the flip deadline (meridian + your NINA 'max minutes after meridian') the window opens. Arriving early lets the flip run through NINA's normal path before the tracking-stop guard fires.

data.name: Settings_ProbeGate_Check
data.value: Defer recovery probes while the guide channel is unstable

data.name: Settings_ProbeGate_Help
data.value: A 300s probe deserves a stable guide channel. The Agent grades stability from several independent signals together (frames flowing, star held over time, per-frame star errors, PHD2 alerts) — a momentary re-lock is not enough. While the channel is declared not ready, the timed probe slides — never beyond a hard 15-minute ceiling, so the sky is always checked eventually. Recovery-hint probes are never delayed.

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Check
data.value: Report unsafe sooner when the guide star fades

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Polls
data.value: Guide-star fade → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_Tip_SkyDegradePolls
data.value: How long the guide channel must keep seeing a faded star before it alone declares UNSAFE. Deliberately SEPARATE from the setting above: that one measures how long the sky stays bad as seen by the imaging camera, this one measures how fast the guide channel reacts. Raising one must not slow the other. 1 poll = the polling interval (default 15 s).

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Help
data.value: The guide star is sampled every few seconds; the imaging camera only once per exposure. When clouds roll in, the guide channel sees it minutes before the next light frame can — and meanwhile the sequence keeps exposing frames that will be discarded. With this on, a sustained collapse of the guide-star signal counts toward unsafe straight away. It can only ever bring unsafe closer, never safe: one star can testify that the sky went bad, not that the whole field came back — that stays the job of the verification exposure.

data.name: Settings_Index_Check
data.value: Use transparency index persistence (recommended)

data.name: Settings_Index_Help
data.value: Accumulates degradation while the transparency index is low and drains it while the sky is clear; brief HAZE bounces no longer reset the cloud timer. Unchecked = legacy logic (consecutive CLOUD polls on the discrete state).

data.name: Settings_ManageExt_Check
data.value: Also manage an Agent not started by the plugin

data.name: Settings_ManageExt_Help
data.value: On (default): when NINA closes, the plugin gracefully shuts down any reachable Agent — even one it did not start — so the PHD2 baseline is always restored. Turn it off if you run the Agent standalone and want it to outlive NINA. Note: for an external Agent there is no process handle — if it hangs, only the Agent's own orphan recovery cleans up at next start.

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Body
data.value: That single instruction is the complete recovery loop: while conditions are unsafe it takes verification exposures at the configured cadence (or sooner on the guide-SNR hint) and ends on its own when the monitor returns SAFE — imaging then resumes automatically. No extra containers or Camera instructions are needed.

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Intro
data.value: To let the session resume by itself after clouds, add ONE instruction to your Advanced Sequence:

data.value: Stale → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_Stale_Check
data.value: Report unsafe on stale telemetry under a degraded sky

data.name: Settings_Stale_Help
data.value: If NINA telemetry stops arriving (beyond the adaptive freshness window — the normal gap between exposures does NOT trigger this) while the session is active and the last known sky was degraded, the monitor escalates to unsafe instead of silently disabling cloud safety.

data.name: Settings_StarLost_Help
data.value: How long STAR_LOST must persist before the monitor reports unsafe. Default 5 minutes (300). Allowed range: 30–1800. Higher values reduce false positives at the cost of slower detection; lower values risk triggering on transient STAR_LOST events the Agent would have recovered.

data.name: Settings_StarLost_Label
data.value: Sky Conditions — STAR_LOST consolidation (seconds)

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Check
data.value: Telemetry forwarding enabled

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Help
data.value: On every saved exposure, sends HFR, star count and image statistics to the Agent (HTTP POST). Optional: if the Agent is offline nothing happens and NINA is never disturbed. Disable to send no data.

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Label
data.value: Forward NINA per-exposure metrics to the Agent

data.name: Settings_Tip_AccumBelow
data.value: While the transparency index (0–1) is below this value, degradation accumulates. Higher = more sensitive to veils. Default matches the Agent's CLOUD threshold (0.5).

data.name: Settings_Tip_AgentLostPolls
data.value: Polls with the Agent unreachable before declaring UNSAFE. Escalates only during an active session — with guiding intentionally stopped, an offline Agent raises no alarm.

data.name: Settings_Tip_ClearPolls
data.value: Polls of clear sky needed to fully drain a saturated accumulator and clear the cloud UNSAFE. Higher = slower, more cautious return to safe.

data.name: Settings_Tip_DegradedPolls
data.value: Accumulated polls of degraded sky before declaring UNSAFE: clear sky drains the count, HAZE is neutral (no reset). Higher = more tolerant of brief veils. 1 poll = the polling interval (default 15 s).

data.name: Settings_Tip_DrainAbove
data.value: While the index is at or above this value, accumulated degradation drains; between the two thresholds (HAZE) nothing changes. Lower = faster recovery to safe.

data.name: Settings_Tip_StalePolls
data.value: Polls with stale telemetry (beyond the adaptive freshness window — the normal gap between exposures never counts) before UNSAFE. Escalates only with cloud safety on, an active session and the last known sky degraded.
